title: Artifacts example test: Docker cleanup must run from an EXIT trap, not trailing commands
answers: artifacts example CI job leaves Docker containers or images behind after failure
docker compose down skipped when the mlflow artifacts example fails
missing docker compose logs in CI when the example test fails
cleanup not running after test_mlflow_artifacts_example exits early
body:
Symptom: When the artifacts example integration test fails on GitHub Actions, downloaded images and containers are not removed, and compose logs are missing from the failure output.
Root cause: tests/tracking/test_mlflow_artifacts.py:test_mlflow_artifacts_example ran `docker compose logs` and `docker compose down {rmi_option}` as plain trailing commands, so any earlier `exit` skipped them.
Fix pattern: Use `set -e` and register one `trap '...' EXIT` that captures `status=$?`, runs logs and down, ORs each failing step into `status=1`, and ends with `exit "$status"`.
Constraints: The trap must run exactly once on every exit path, including exhausted pull retries. A cleanup failure may only raise a zero status to nonzero; it must not overwrite a nonzero application status. Keep `rmi_option` (`--rmi all` on GitHub Actions) inside the trap.
applies: Shell script built inside test_mlflow_artifacts_example; any new step added to that script that can exit early should rely on the same trap.
says: The artifact example automated test does not clean up containers when it fails.
Integration test failures for the artifact example are missing diagnostic service logs.
Please make the artifact sample test remove downloaded images even after crashes.
Build logs show no console output from services when the artifact test aborts.
Leftover test containers remain behind after the artifact sample pipeline step exits.
search: In tests/tracking/test_mlflow_artifacts.py:test_mlflow_artifacts_example, Docker cleanup and compose logs must run from an EXIT trap rather than trailing commands so failures do not leave containers or skip logs. The trap registers with set -e, captures status=$?, runs docker compose logs and docker compose down with rmi_option (--rmi all on GitHub Actions), ORs each failing step into status=1, and exits with status. It applies to the shell script in test_mlflow_artifacts_example and any new early-exit step, running once on every exit path while cleanup failures may only raise zero status to nonzero without overwriting a nonzero application status.
